paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: This pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical problems across various educational levels and subjects. The chart comprises 12 slices, each labeled with a specific subject area and educational level, along with a percentage and number in parentheses. The slices, listed in order of their apparent size, are as follows: Algebra - Olympiad-level, colored blue, accounts for 21.19%; Pre-Calculus - High School, colored salmon, accounts for 14.21%; Algebra - High School, colored green, accounts for 17.83%; Combinatorics - Olympiad-level, colored orange, accounts for 9.56%; Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra - University-level, colored brown, and Geometry - Olympiad-level, colored gray, both account for 6.46%; Calculus and Analysis - University-level, colored teal, accounts for 6.20%; Probability - University-level, colored pink, accounts for 5.43%; Statistics - University-level, colored cyan, accounts for 4.39%; Differential Equations - University-level, colored purple, accounts for 3.62%; Geometry - High School, colored light purple, accounts for 3.62%; and Number Theory - Olympiad-level, colored yellow, accounts for 1.03%. The chart includes a label and percentage for each slice, with no additional legend or visual emphasis. The slices appear to be arranged in descending order of size.
